# Fabric decision record

## Decision

Stage D as the legacy-compatible bridge, then cut over to B only after ownership, rollback, recovery, and isolation gates pass; A remains a bounded warm-workload optimization and C is rejected.

This is not a universal performance ranking. B is the phase-2 target because the supplied security finding supports workspace-only mounts and scoped credentials. D is only a deadline bridge. A may be used only for explicitly warm workloads after its incident and bind controls pass. C's invalid pooled distribution is excluded rather than revived as a throughput claim.

| phase | option | owner | purpose | gates | rollback triggers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | D | Migration Lead | Provide the required legacy-compatible bridge within 14 days while preserving the pre-D state for rollback. | G-D-MIGRATION, G-OWNERS, G-ROLLBACK, G-D-RECOVERY | RT-D-DEADLINE, RT-D-RECOVERY |
| 2 | B | Execution Fabric Operations Lead | Cut over from D to B only after security, ownership, recovery, and rollback evidence is executable and passing. | G-B-ISOLATION, G-B-OWNERS, G-B-ROLLBACK | RT-B-ISOLATION, RT-B-RECOVERY |

The decision depends on `D-MIGRATION`, `D-RECOVERY`, `B-ISOLATION`, `B-MIGRATION`, `CON-MIGRATION`, `CON-OWNER`, and `CON-ROLLBACK`.

### Conditional optimization

Option A is eligible only when all of the following remain true:

- The workload is explicitly warm and benchmarked separately from cold runs.
- `CTRL-A-CLEANUP` passes an owner-token and PID/name-reuse cleanup test.
- `CTRL-A-BIND` passes structured bind-validation tests.
- Named ownership and rollback gates remain satisfied.

The traced evidence is `BM-A-WARM`, `BM-A-COLD`, `INC-A-CLEANUP`, `SEC-A-BIND`, `CON-OWNER`, and `CON-ROLLBACK`.

## Claim ledger

| claim_id | disposition | evidence | condition | confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A-WARM | supported | PROP-A,BM-A-WARM,BM-B-WARM,BM-D-WARM | For the supplied warm workload only, comparing valid A, B, and D series with n=3 each; the invalid pooled C series is excluded. | medium |
| A-COLD | unknown | PROP-A,BM-A-COLD | For the supplied cold workload, whose A series has n=3, a 200 ms median, and one censored observation; no acceptance threshold is supplied. | low |
| B-ISOLATION | supported | PROP-B,SEC-B-ISOLATION | Within the supplied security findings, provided B retains workspace-only mounts and scoped credentials; no cross-provider comparison was supplied. | medium |
| B-MIGRATION | unknown | PROP-B,CON-MIGRATION | Immediate migration to B, rather than migration through the required legacy-compatible stage within 14 days. | low |
| C-THROUGHPUT | rejected | PROP-C,BM-C-POOLED | Universal throughput inferred from the supplied pooled-warm-cold series. | high |
| D-MIGRATION | conditionally supported | PROP-D,CON-MIGRATION | D is used only as a legacy-compatible bridge and must pass the day-14 compatibility gate; the proposal is the only supplied support for feasibility. | low |
| D-RECOVERY | unknown | PROP-D,INC-D-RECOVERY | Recovery ownership and readiness for D; the observed incident instead records delayed recovery and no assigned owner. | unknown |
| CON-MIGRATION | required | CON-MIGRATION | Every decision must provide a legacy-compatible stage within 14 days. | high |
| CON-OWNER | required | CON-OWNER | Named cleanup and recovery owners are required before any cutover. | high |
| CON-ROLLBACK | required | CON-ROLLBACK | Every cutover requires a testable rollback trigger and preserved prior state. | high |

The A cold boundary remains unknown because no acceptable cold-latency threshold or censored-run outcome is supplied. B's immediate-migration claim remains unknown because the constraint states the required result but does not prove a direct-B rehearsal. D recovery remains unknown because the incident contradicts complete ownership. C is rejected with high confidence because its source distribution is explicitly invalid for the claimed inference.

## Benchmark distributions

| evidence_id | proposal | workload | samples | censored | valid | median_ms | exclusion_reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BM-A-WARM | A | warm | 3 | 0 | true | 40 | - |
| BM-A-COLD | A | cold | 3 | 1 | true | 200 | - |
| BM-B-WARM | B | warm | 3 | 0 | true | 70 | - |
| BM-B-COLD | B | cold | 3 | 0 | true | 95 | - |
| BM-C-POOLED | C | pooled-warm-cold | 4 | 0 | false | - | workload-mixed samples cannot support one throughput distribution |
| BM-D-WARM | D | warm | 3 | 0 | true | 85 | - |
| BM-D-COLD | D | cold | 3 | 0 | true | 125 | - |

Medians are retained only for valid series. Sample counts describe recorded latency samples; `censored` is recorded separately and is not silently added to the sample count. The invalid C series has no declared median in the decision record.

## Alternatives

| option | disposition | bounded counterexample | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | bounded conditional optimization | A has the lowest observed warm median at 40 ms with n=3, but its cold median is 200 ms with one censored observation and it remains ineligible until cleanup authorization and bind-validation controls pass. | BM-A-WARM, BM-A-COLD, INC-A-CLEANUP, SEC-A-BIND |
| B | selected target after D bridge and gates | B's supplied isolation is supported, but its 70 ms warm median is slower than A's 40 ms warm median and no evidence establishes immediate migration. | PROP-B, SEC-B-ISOLATION, CON-MIGRATION, BM-B-WARM, BM-A-WARM |
| C | rejected | The only supplied C benchmark mixes warm and cold samples, is invalid, and cannot establish universal throughput even though two individual samples are low. | PROP-C, BM-C-POOLED |
| D | stage-1 migration bridge only | D addresses legacy compatibility as a bridge, but recovery was delayed because no recovery owner was assigned; it is not a proven recovery-complete target. | PROP-D, INC-D-RECOVERY, CON-OWNER, BM-D-WARM, BM-D-COLD |

## Constraints and controls

| constraint_id | status | gate_id |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CON-MIGRATION | satisfied-by-stage-1 | G-D-MIGRATION |
| CON-OWNER | gated | G-OWNERS |
| CON-ROLLBACK | gated | G-ROLLBACK |

| control_id | owner | evidence | decision effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CTRL-A-CLEANUP | Execution Fabric Operations Lead | INC-A-CLEANUP | A is ineligible until cleanup requires an unforgeable owner token and a PID/name-reuse test proves peer resources cannot be removed. |
| CTRL-D-RECOVERY | Migration Lead | INC-D-RECOVERY | D cannot start and B cannot cut over until a recovery owner and alternate are named and a timed recovery drill passes. |
| CTRL-A-BIND | Security Engineering Lead | SEC-A-BIND | A is ineligible until bind requests use structured validation that rejects paths and modes outside the approved workspace policy. |
| CTRL-B-ISOLATION | Security Engineering Lead | SEC-B-ISOLATION | B remains eligible only while acceptance tests prove workspace-only mounts and scoped credentials; a failure blocks or rolls back cutover. |

## Executable gates

| gate_id | phase | check | expected result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| G-D-MIGRATION | 1 | Execute the legacy-compatibility acceptance suite and compare recorded completion with approved migration start plus 14 calendar days. | All legacy cases pass and completion is no later than day 14. |
| G-OWNERS | 1 | Inspect the cutover roster and page primary and alternate cleanup and recovery owners during rehearsal. | Named primary and alternate owners acknowledge before cutover approval. |
| G-ROLLBACK | 1 | Run a staged rollback from D while retaining pre-D state, then rerun the legacy-compatibility suite. | Prior state is restored and every legacy case passes. |
| G-D-RECOVERY | 1 | Run a timed D recovery drill led by the assigned recovery owner and record restoration and validation results. | Recovery meets an objective approved before execution and restored state passes validation. |
| G-B-ISOLATION | 2 | Enumerate B mount targets and credential scopes in isolation and compare them with workspace and least-privilege allowlists. | Every mount is workspace-only, every credential is task-scoped, and no unexpected target or scope exists. |
| G-B-OWNERS | 2 | Repeat the owner-page rehearsal immediately before B cutover. | Named primary and alternate cleanup and recovery owners acknowledge before cutover. |
| G-B-ROLLBACK | 2 | Run a staged B-to-D rollback while retaining validated D state, then rerun isolation and compatibility checks on restored D. | D state is restored, legacy cases pass, and B credentials are revoked. |

## Rollback triggers

| trigger_id | check | condition | action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| RT-D-DEADLINE | Review the dated migration milestone report daily. | A milestone projects compatible completion later than day 14. | Halt D expansion, retain the current legacy state, and correct the migration plan. |
| RT-D-RECOVERY | Run G-D-RECOVERY and verify owner acknowledgement. | No recovery owner acknowledges, or a drill fails its approved objective or state validation. | Stop cutover and restore preserved pre-D state. |
| RT-B-ISOLATION | Continuously compare mounts and credential scopes with approved allowlists. | A mount escapes the workspace or a credential exceeds approved task scope. | Block or reverse B, revoke B credentials, and restore preserved D state. |
| RT-B-RECOVERY | Run the recovery drill at cutover and after provider or state-format changes. | The recovery owner is unavailable, or restoration misses its approved objective or validation. | Stop B expansion and restore preserved D state under the assigned owner. |

## Unknown boundaries

| unknown_id | status | evidence | missing evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| UNK-RECOVERY-OWNERSHIP | unknown | INC-D-RECOVERY, CON-OWNER | Named primary and alternate recovery owners, an approved recovery objective, and successful timed D and B recovery drills with preserved prior state. |
| UNK-PROVIDER-BOUNDARIES | unknown | SEC-B-ISOLATION, SEC-A-BIND | Provider-specific evidence for mount enforcement, credential revocation, failure isolation, state persistence, and recovery semantics. |
| UNK-A-COLD-ACCEPTANCE | unknown | BM-A-COLD | A cold-latency acceptance objective and the outcome and censoring mechanism for the single censored A cold observation. |

## Evidence refresh

| trigger_id | category | condition | action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ER-IDENTITY-CHANGE | identity | Provider, workspace identity model, mount construction, credential issuer, or credential scopes change. | Rerun provider-specific isolation, structured-bind, mount-boundary, credential-scope, and revocation tests; reassess B and A before further cutover. |
| ER-BENCHMARK-WINDOW | window | Workload mix or measurement window changes, a benchmark is older than 30 days at a decision gate, or an approved latency objective changes. | Collect warm and cold distributions separately, retain counts and censoring, recompute medians, and reassess without pooling. |
| ER-FABRIC-INCIDENT | incident | Cleanup removes a peer resource, recovery is delayed, a mount escapes the workspace, or a credential exceeds approved scope. | Freeze the affected option, preserve logs and state, rerun related controls, and reopen the decision before resuming. |

## Source identities

- `PROP-A`, `PROP-B`, `PROP-C`, and `PROP-D` identify the four public proposal documents.
- `BM-*` identifiers resolve to `evidence/benchmarks/raw.json`; `INC-*` identifiers resolve to `evidence/incidents/incidents.json`; and `SEC-*` identifiers resolve to `evidence/security/findings.json` through `evidence/index.json`.
- `CON-MIGRATION`, `CON-OWNER`, and `CON-ROLLBACK` resolve to `constraints.json`.
